title: Identification of Unique Pd-based Compounds in Twisted MoTe2 Nanojunctions
content: Introducing superconductivity in topological materials can lead to innovative electronic phases and device functionalities. Recent observations of fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted bilayer molybdenum ditelluride have confirmed the existence of fractional Chern insulators in the absence of magnetic fields. In principle, the creation of superconductivity in fractional Chern insulators can lead to interesting electronic states of matter under unexplored experimental conditions. However, creating superconductivity using traditional means in such air-sensitive two-dimensional (2D) moiré materials is challenging. [1-6] We overcome such challenges by presenting a unique strategy for constructing high-quality superconducting junctions consisting of air-sensitive van der Waals moiré materials, such as twisted bilayer MoTe2 [1-3]. We present systematic characterizations of the junction, including both the atomic structure and the electronic transport behaviors. The key to our approach to fabricating high-quality superconducting moiré junctions is the recently introduced on-chip 2D growth mechanism based on the unexpected discovery of rapid mass transport, and crystal growth templated on 2D materials [2]. We use this approach to find that a class of unique Pd-based compounds produced on topological chalcogenides are superconductors [1, 2]. Here, we demonstrated atomic-resolution visualization of a complicated compound (Pd7MoTe2) with high crystalline quality by using high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) (no serious beam damage issue [7-9]).
